title: How Far is Adam from Natural Gradient Descent?
abstract: arXiv:2610.00004v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Adam is the standard optimizer in deep learning, yet its geometric relationship to natural gradient descent (NGD) contains unresolved questions. We study Adam's full update rule, including momentum, as a diagonal empirical Fisher approximation subject to diagonal truncation, empirical label substitution, and temporal lag. Using the scale-invariant $\gamma(\Delta\theta)$ metric, we measure Adam's geometric deviation from true NGD across four loss landscapes: well-conditioned linear regression, ill-conditioned linear regression, logistic regression, and a non-convex small neural network. Adam's geometric trajectory is context-dependent. Deviation remains low in well-conditioned settings but rises significantly under ill-conditioning, reaching misalignments of $\approx 10^3$ in the neural network. translated_title: Adam距离自然梯度下降有多远？
translated_abstract: Adam是深度学习中的标准优化器，然而它与自然梯度下降（NGD）之间的几何关系仍存在未解决的问题。我们将Adam的完整更新规则（包括动量）视为一种对角经验Fisher近似来加以研究，该近似受到对角截断、经验标签替代以及时间滞后等因素的影响。利用尺度不变的γ(Δθ)度量，我们在四种损失景观上测量了Adam与真实NGD之间的几何偏差：良态线性回归、病态线性回归、逻辑回归以及一个非凸的小型神经网络。Adam的几何轨迹依赖于具体情境：在良态设置下偏差保持较低，但在病态条件下显著上升，在神经网络中失准程度达到约10^3。更大的几何漂移与较慢的初期优化相关，但并不会损害最终的目标函数最小化；Adam始终能够达到……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文用尺度不变的几何度量首次系统量化了包含动量的Adam与真实自然梯度下降的偏差，发现该偏差在良态问题中很小、在病态问题中急剧增大（神经网络中可达约10^3），且几何漂移只会拖慢初期优化速度、不影响最终的损失最小化效果。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically quantifies the geometric deviation of Adam's full update rule (including momentum) from true natural gradient descent using a scale-invariant metric, showing the deviation stays small in well-conditioned problems but grows dramatically under ill-conditioning (up to ≈10^3 in a neural network), and that larger geometric drift only slows early optimization without degrading final loss minimization.
